buildSourceNote: Build 144 carries v1.1.0-rc.21. The owner reported 'why it is not updating in realtime, abdul gani's punches showing as 10 but last login signin is not recorded'. THE STALENESS WAS REAL AND WAS MY GAP: StaffActivityHub fetched once on mount (useEffect with [load]) and NEVER polled, so anything happening while it was open - a punch, a sign-in, an action - stayed invisible until someone pressed Refresh, which makes a report about live systems read as stale. It now polls every 60s, matching the app's notifications poll rather than its 10s operational dashboards because this is monthly aggregate reporting over 61 accounts plus five grouped aggregates rather than a live queue; the poll is skipped while the tab is hidden, uses a silent path that does not flip the loading flag so it cannot flash or blank the table mid-read, refreshes an open drill-down too, and the header now states when the data was fetched. The polling effect is declared AFTER openDetail on purpose - the dependency array is evaluated during render, so referencing it earlier would hit the temporal dead zone. THE SECOND HALF WAS A DATA-SEMANTICS QUESTION, AND BOTH NUMBERS WERE CORRECT: ABDUL GANI SHEK (dev-206, user 51, employee_id 1, role BD ASSISTANT/ DRIVER) has 10 attendance punches (2026-09-05 to 2026-09-16, all Present) and zero login_history rows. Three INDEPENDENT systems record these: attendance in workforce_attendance keyed on employee_id, sign-ins in login_history keyed on user_id and only recorded from 2026-09-16 06:36:06Z (12:06 IST), and actions in jc_activity_log / security_audit_logs. A punch does not imply a sign-in. His punches all predate the cutover and his most recent one was written at 03:51:22Z = 09:21 IST, before recording began and on a session already open, so it produced no login row. The banner now leads with that independence rather than only explaining the date. FOUND AND DELIBERATELY NOT CHANGED: check_in is the IST wall-clock and normally matches created_at converted to IST (2026-09-08: check_in 09:38 vs created 04:08:37Z), but attendance_id 40 and 36 both carry check_in 13:07 while their created_at convert to 09:21 and 09:18 IST - the same value on two different days suggests a manual EDIT_ATTENDANCE_TIME, which the endpoint supports. Editing a punch time is legitimate so it is flagged rather than corrected, but it means a punch time cannot always be re-derived from the row's creation time. See docs/CHANGELOG.md. PRIOR BUILDS: 143 carried rc.20, 142 carried rc.19, 141 carried rc.17 and rc.18, 139 carried rc.15 and rc.16. The owner asked 'LAST SIGNIN SHOWS NEVER RECORDED ?' and the answer was: that is correct behaviour, and it is provable. The viewer's own session (user_id 30, developer) carries an iat of 2026-09-16T06:10:59Z, decoded out of the browser rather than inferred, while login recording went live at 06:36:06Z when rc.15 applied migration 32 - so the session was issued 25 MINUTES BEFORE THE FEATURE EXISTED, and because a session is a 24-hour JWT no new sign-in had happened since. login_history held 6 rows including FOUR real successful sign-ins that day (users 94, 29, 21, 55), so recording demonstrably worked, and both jwt.sign sites that mint a session were checked to be instrumented so no login path was missed. The screen explained itself badly and that was MINE: the banner was gated on rows.every(r => !r.last_login_at), so the instant a few people signed in the condition went false and THE EXPLANATION DISAPPEARED, leaving a bare 'Never recorded' with no context for everyone else - now gated on .some(...) so it persists while any account is unexplained; the copy now gives the real reason (24-hour session tokens) and names the exact cutover time rather than only 'recording started today'; and the viewer's own row is marked 'you' and reads 'This session predates recording' with a tooltip, instead of the identical bare text everyone else gets. TO POPULATE YOUR OWN ROW: sign out and sign back in. Nothing else is needed. ALSO VERIFIED END TO END IN THE LIVE UI while diagnosing, which closes out rc.19's timezone work: HR DAPL renders 1:09 pm (07:39:18Z), MUSTAFA 1:10 pm (07:40:00Z), sayeed 1:08 pm (07:38:31Z), SHASHI KUMAR 1:05 pm (07:35:51Z) and Suryakant 12:15 pm (06:45:20Z) - all correct IST, where every one of them previously read 5h30m early. See docs/CHANGELOG.md. PRIOR BUILDS: 142 carried rc.19 (the timezone fix), 141 carried rc.17 and rc.18, 139 carried rc.15 and rc.16. The stack is UTC end to end - Cloud SQL reports @@system_time_zone UTC with NOW() == UTC_TIMESTAMP() and the container is UTC - while the site and the viewer are Asia/Kolkata, UTC+05:30. src/db/index.ts sets dateStrings true, so MySQL returns DATETIME/TIMESTAMP as '2026-09-16 06:45:20' with NO timezone marker, and JavaScript parses a bare string like that as LOCAL time: measured in the live browser, new Date('2026-09-16 06:45:20') resolves to 2026-09-16T01:15:20Z, 5h30m EARLY. A sign-in that really happened at 12:15 IST displayed as 06:45. A BLANKET FIX WAS WRITTEN AND THEN REVERTED AFTER CHECKING THE DATA: an Express json replacer labelling every YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss as UTC would have repaired some 300 call sites at once, but this schema holds BOTH KINDS in the SAME table. job_card_master.created_at and updated_at span hours 0-6 (UTC instants, i.e. 09:30-15:30 IST) while crm_arrival_at, crm_jc_started_at and crm_jc_completed_at hold 10:00, 11:15, 15:15, 17:30 (LOCAL WALL-CLOCK, because /api/job-cards/:no/crm-timestamps parses the literal CRM digits specifically to avoid Date() re-interpreting them - its own comment says 'Wall-clock, never an instant'). Labelling those wall-clock columns as UTC would have shifted them +5h30m and broken values that read correctly today. FIXED INSTEAD, SURGICALLY: the three fields that are genuine instants (login_history.login_at, jc_activity_log.created_at, security_audit_logs.created_at, all written by NOW() or CURRENT_TIMESTAMP) now carry the Z; the report's calendar maths uses the SITE timezone rather than the server's UTC clock, because working-days-elapsed and this-month disagreed with the shop floor for the first 5h30m of every day; and StaffActivityHub formats explicitly in Asia/Kolkata rather than the viewer's device, so the same event cannot read differently on two machines, with the punch list labelled as gate wall-clock and deliberately NOT converted. VERIFIED LIVE THROUGH THE OWNER'S OWN SESSION: GET /api/admin/user-activity/staff now returns login_at 2026-09-16T06:45:20Z, which renders as 12:15 IST where it previously showed 06:45, and working_days_elapsed 14 for September - correct for 1-16 Sep excluding two Sundays. STILL OPEN AND NEEDING A DECISION RATHER THAN A SWEEP: about 300 call sites in 97 files still render a bare DB datetime through new Date(v).toLocaleString(), so most screens still show instants 5h30m early - gate_out_time 2026-09-06 22:15:00 UTC is really 07 Sep 03:45 IST and displays as 22:15. The correct fix is to classify EVERY datetime column once as instant-or-wall-clock and normalise on that basis, which is a schema-semantics exercise, not a regex. PRIOR BUILDS: 141 carried rc.17 and rc.18, 139 carried rc.15 and rc.16. rc.17 and rc.18 are BOTH navigation defects the owner hit while actually using the app, and both were MINE. rc.17: Staff Activity had shipped in rc.15 with its ROLE_TABS entries, its render block and its server gate, but was never added to WORKSPACE_MAPPING in AppShell.tsx - and the sub-nav renders only tabs whose mapping equals the active workspace, so an unmapped tab matched NO workspace, appeared in no menu at all, and could only be opened by typing /staff-activity. Reported as 'where can i find staff activity'. Mapped to 'hr' and verified in the served bundle. Every other tab id in App.tsx (44 of them) was audited against the map: the only one without a mapping is 'logout-deep-link', the intentional Logout pseudo-tab, so this was a single mistake rather than a class. Note for future tabs: src/lib/tabRoutes.ts needs NO change (a tab id IS its path) but WORKSPACE_MAPPING does. rc.18: the header search input had no value, no onChange, no handler and no state - it had NEVER been wired, and typing in it did nothing. Reported as 'what use it of that search tab on the top besides back button'. It is now a jump-to-screen launcher over permittedTabs only, so it needs no new endpoint, no new permission and no data semantics, and because it can only reach screens the role already has it cannot become an access path. The broader search (job cards by number or VRN, people, vehicles) needs endpoint and matching decisions and is deliberately left open rather than half-built. Prior builds: 139 carried rc.15 and rc.16, 140 carried rc.17. rc.15 adds staff activity reporting and CORRECTS A SERIOUS ERROR OF MINE THAT HAD A SECURITY CONSEQUENCE. The owner asked 'can i also see the user activity like his compliance report, when did he login did he punched attendance, how much active he is', visible 'only to the developer and gm service and hr/admin'. NEW: GET /api/admin/user-activity/staff and /:userId, implemented in src/api/routes/user-activity.routes.ts and mounted via createUserActivityRouter (the auth helpers are closure-local in server.ts); screen StaffActivityHub.tsx at /staff-activity, registered for admin, developer and gm_service ONLY - there is NO 'hr' role in `roles`, the HR account hr_dapl carries 'admin'. Assembled from five grouped queries merged in JS rather than one wide join, because the sources key on employee_id, user_id and actor_user_id differently and a join multiplies rows, producing counts that look plausible and are wrong. Attendance queries list columns explicitly because workforce_attendance carries face_photo_in and face_photo_out as LONGTEXT base64. NEW, AND IT WAS THE ACTUAL BLOCKER: logins were never recorded, and login_history could NEVER have recorded them - user_id is NOT NULL with an FK to `users`, but the app authenticates against user_access_master and only 19 of 61 accounts exist in `users`. The HR/admin account (29), the security agent (45), the biller (50) and the advisor (95) are ALL absent from `users`, so every insert would have failed with ER_NO_REFERENCED_ROW. Migration 32 (login_history_relax_fk) drops that FK and adds idx_login_history_user_time. /api/auth/login and /api/auth/verify-otp now record success AND failure, and the write never throws - an audit side-effect must not deny a valid user access. There is NO BACKFILL, deliberately: past sign-ins are unrecoverable, so last_login_at is null for almost everyone until they sign in once, and the UI says 'Never recorded' with a banner rather than inventing history. THE ERROR: in rc.13 I added 'reception' to GATE_OUT_SECURITY_ROLES while stating that production had ZERO security_agent accounts. THAT WAS FALSE. suryakant (user 45) is an active security_agent with a valid bcrypt password and must_change_password 0. My probe counted security users through a LEFT JOIN onto `roles` and returned 0, and I trusted that count without querying the account table directly - a zero from a join is evidence about the join, not about the world. The consequence was real: a front-desk role was handed the ability to RELEASE A VEHICLE. The true defect was never a missing account - security_agent was ALREADY in GATE_OUT_SECURITY_ROLES, so the API always accepted it, but ROLE_TABS.security_agent had no security-workspace tab, and the only caller of POST /api/gate-out/gate-out in the whole repository is SecurityWorkspace.tsx:63, rendered solely on that tab id. The role held the authority and could not exercise it. rc.15 gives security_agent AND gate_personnel the tab, and REMOVES 'reception' from both GATE_OUT_SECURITY_ROLES and ROLE_TABS.reception. The journey is unaffected: the GM (sayeed_dp) holds security-workspace and cashier-workspace. ALSO FIXED in rc.15: EmployeePerformanceHub's 'Completed' column read 0 for every employee forever, because it compared job_status to the literal 'completed', which the enum cannot hold; it now uses isWorkCompleteStatus(), and the name match is trimmed and case-insensitive because production stores names like 'ranjeet ' with a trailing space. rc.16 fixes a defect ONLY LIVE TESTING COULD REVEAL: the first recorded login carried ip_address 169.254.169.126, a link-local internal hop, because Express with trust proxy 1 resolves req.ip to the LAST X-Forwarded-For entry while Cloud Run puts the real client FIRST. It now takes the leftmost entry, and the comment records that the value is a client-supplied claim which must never drive an authorisation or rate-limiting decision. See docs/CHANGELOG.md.

STILL OPEN, PRODUCTION-WIDE, FOUND WHILE VERIFYING rc.14: the rc1 workforce profile never applies. .dockerignore and .gcloudignore both exclude '.env' and '.env.*', and .env.rc1 is gitignored as well, so VITE_WORKFORCE_PROFILE is undefined at build time and every 'import.meta.env.VITE_WORKFORCE_PROFILE === rc1' check in the codebase is permanently false - the App.tsx tab guard AND AttendanceShiftLog.tsx. Confirmed against the live bundle: zero occurrences of 'rc1', zero of 'dev', and the excluded-tabs array literal absent. Net effect today is permissive (nothing is hidden), so it is NOT an outage, but it means the production-hardening configuration is documentation rather than behaviour. Needs an OWNER DECISION: either pass VITE_WORKFORCE_PROFILE via a Docker ARG/ENV or a Cloud Build substitution so it survives the context exclusion, or accept that rc1 is inert and delete the dead checks. '.env.*' must stay dockerignored either way - excluding env files from the image is the right instinct, and .env.rc1 merely happens to carry no secret.
